exposure: Cervical dilation at neuraxial analgesia initiation (≤3 cm or >3 cm)
Timing of neuraxial analgesia initiation (early vs. late)
outcome: Duration of delivery (first and second stage)
Rates of instrumental and cesarean deliveries
cohort: 297 multiparous women undergoing elective induction of labor with combined spinal-epidural analgesia
finding: Early initiation of neuraxial analgesia in electively induced labor in multiparous women did not prolong the duration of delivery.
mod_finding: The study found that early initiation of neuraxial analgesia in electively induced labor did not prolong the duration of delivery, and there was no significant difference in the rates of instrumental or cesarean deliveries between the early and late groups.
